newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahraini court continues trial of coup suspects.
newsitem.headline: Bahraini court continues trial of coup suspects.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court on Saturday continued the trial of 81 people accused of involvement in an alleged Iranian-backed plot to topple Bahrain's government, lawyers said.
The trial of the suspects -- 59 in court and the rest tried in absentia -- began in the Gulf Arab state on March 1. The trial was halted on Thursday and Friday for the Moslem weekend.
Lawyers said some verdicts could be passed in the next week and some suspects could face the death penalty.

The defendants are accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
Political parties are banned in Bahrain. Bahrain in June accused Shi'ite Moslem Iran of backing an attempt to overthrow the government. Iran denied the allegation.

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community seeking political and economic reform by the Sunni rulers have waged a campaign of bombings, arson, sabotage and riots since December 1994. At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested.
